# Phase 01 — Application Foundation — Review Record

The seven lenses `phases/phase-01-application-foundation.md` requires, run as
independent read-only reviewers against the packet, `contracts/review-gates.md`,
the owned requirements and `reviews/phase-01-evidence.md`. No reviewer was told
to preserve the implementation.

Severity follows `contracts/review-gates.md`. `BLOCKER`, `CRITICAL` and `HIGH`
prevent `PASS`. `MEDIUM` must be fixed or explicitly accepted with justification
and tracking. `LOW` and `NOTE` may remain if tracked.

Every finding was verified or disproved before any remediation, as
`REQ-EXEC-171` requires. **Status** records that verification:

- `CONFIRMED` — reproduced, or established by reading the code against the
  requirement.
- `CONFIRMED (latent)` — the defect is real and reachable by a caller that does
  not exist yet, so it harms no user today.
- `REJECTED` — investigated and shown not to hold. The reasoning is recorded.

**Disposition** records what was done. It is filled in as remediation lands, and
no finding is closed on the reviewer's word alone.

## Lenses run

| Lens | Findings | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | 15 | 5 HIGH |
| Code Quality / Maintainability | 17 + 4 notes | 2 HIGH |
| Testing / Regression | 18 | 2 HIGH |
| UX / Accessibility / Input | 20 | 1 CRITICAL, 6 HIGH |
| Security / Privacy | 10 | 2 HIGH |
| Browser / Platform Compatibility | 17 | 2 HIGH |
| Adversarial Agent-Quality | 19 | 5 HIGH |

Several findings were raised by more than one lens independently. Those are
merged here under one identifier and the lenses are listed together, because a
defect found three times is one defect.

## Blocking findings

### F-01 — CRITICAL — No portalled surface is themed at all

*Lenses:* UX/Accessibility. *Status:* CONFIRMED, reproduced in Chromium.

Radix renders every dialogue, menu, tooltip, popover and select into
`document.body`. The theme writes its custom properties onto `.ag-theme-root`,
which is a descendant of `#audiogubbins` and therefore not an ancestor of the
portal. Custom properties inherit down the tree only, so inside a portal every
`var(--ag-…)` is undefined and every declaration reading one is invalid at
computed-value time.

Measured against the production build, with the Settings dialogue open:
`background-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`, `padding: 0px`, `border-radius: 0px`,
`--ag-chrome-surface-overlay` empty, parent chain `DIV.ag-dialog → BODY → HTML`.
The View menu is the same.

The consequences a user meets: the dialogue and the palette have no surface,
padding or corner; a menu has no panel behind it; the highlighted-entry
background does not render, so arrowing through a menu shows nothing moving,
while the `outline: none` on the same rule does apply; a disabled entry is not
dimmed; the light theme leaves every overlay on the hard-coded dark body colour;
and the minimal-motion guard, written to catch third-party animation, cannot
reach the third-party animation it was written for.

axe passed because the portal text sits on the body's hard-coded `#1c1d22` and
meets contrast by accident. `REQ-UX-155`, `REQ-UX-070`, `REQ-UX-005`.

### F-02 — HIGH — No visible focus indicator inside any overlay

*Lenses:* UX/Accessibility. *Status:* CONFIRMED.

`.ag-app :focus-visible` cannot match a portalled element, so no control in the
Settings dialogue or the command palette shows a focus ring — the search field,
the four tabs, the three selects, the two switches, the slider thumb. Radix's own
`outline: none` on a highlighted menu item removes the browser default where it
would otherwise have shown. The test behind the evidence's "the focus position is
visible" claim presses Tab once and lands on a menu-bar trigger, which is inside
`.ag-app`. `REQ-UX-005`, WCAG 2.4.7.

### F-03 — HIGH — The docking adapter fabricates every group's region

*Lenses:* Architecture, Code Quality, Testing, UX/Accessibility. *Status:*
CONFIRMED.

`readLayout` writes `region: DockRegion.Centre` for every group it reads back
from the engine, and computes `proportion` from width alone. The engine reports a
layout change on a drag, a close, a resize and a tab change alike, so after any
interaction the stored layout says every group is centre. On the next mount the
adapter anchors each group after the first `within` the centre, and the user's
left, right and bottom panels return as tabs in one stack. No group height
survives either.

`ADR-0010` states that AudioGubbins stores "which group holds each" and "what
proportion each group takes". The adapter can recover neither and invents a value
rather than reporting that it cannot. `REQ-UX-057`, `REQ-UX-059`,
`REQ-EXEC-136.15`.

### F-04 — HIGH — `REQ-UX-058` is a library, not a feature

*Lenses:* Architecture, Adversarial, UX/Accessibility. *Status:* CONFIRMED.

The requirement states with `shall` that users can create, save, duplicate,
rename, reset, delete and switch rapidly between layouts. Only save-as and reset
have a command. `switchTo`, `rename` and `remove` exist in the store and
`duplicate` in the layout store, with no caller. Five of the six presets can
never be loaded.

The three that do exist combine into a trap: after one save-as, `workspace.reset`
refuses because the layout is no longer built-in and advises deleting it, and
there is no delete command. The user cannot return to any preset without clearing
storage.

### F-05 — HIGH — Custom workspaces are not persisted

*Lenses:* Architecture, Adversarial. *Status:* CONFIRMED.

`createLayoutStore(presets)` never receives the stored user layouts, although the
parameter exists for exactly that, and `persist` writes only the mounted layout.
After a reload the saved workspace is absent from `available` and from the store,
so `rename`, `remove` and `reset` would all refuse on the layout the user is
looking at. A later save-as recomputes its identifier from `available.length`,
so it collides. `REQ-UX-058`, `REQ-UX-059`, `REQ-EXEC-136.11`.

### F-06 — HIGH — The stored-layout validator is incomplete and its result is asserted

*Lenses:* Code Quality. *Status:* CONFIRMED.

`layoutProblem` checks `schemaVersion`, `id`, `displayName` and `groups`. It
never checks `builtIn`, declared non-optional, nor the layout-level
`activePanelId`. `resolveLayout` then writes `stored as WorkspaceLayout` — the
assertion the same file's comment says a validator must never make.

The reachable consequence: a layout whose `activePanelId` names no panel passes
validation and mounts. `workspace.close-panel` is then available, `withoutPanel`
returns a new object because its early return is guarded only by the panel count,
the caller compares object identity, sees a change, persists, remounts the dock
and announces **"The panel is closed."** while nothing closed. Two distinct
failures are collapsed into one identity comparison and the second is reported as
success. `REQ-UX-059`, `REQ-EXEC-136.12`, `REQ-EXEC-136.15`.

### F-07 — HIGH — No shortcut can be remapped

*Lenses:* Architecture, Adversarial, UX/Accessibility, Code Quality. *Status:*
CONFIRMED.

`REQ-UX-066` states "Users must be able to fully remap shortcuts", and names
import and export of profiles and reset to defaults. `rebind`, `unbind`,
`duplicateProfile`, `exportProfile` and `importProfile` are implemented and
tested, and none has a caller in the application. The profile is a module
constant read from six places, with no store. The Shortcuts settings section
tells the user remapping "arrives with the phase that adds a shortcut editor",
which no phase packet schedules. That is silent scope deferral written into the
product's own interface.

### F-08 — HIGH — The consented diagnostic export path does not exist

*Lenses:* Security/Privacy, Architecture, Adversarial. *Status:* CONFIRMED.

WU-01.D requires "structured local logging, diagnostic mode and explicit-consent
export path". `assembleBundle`, `renderBundle` and `describeBundleContents` are
exported and tested, and `grep` for them over `apps/` returns nothing. There is
no export command, no consent dialogue and no contents preview, so
`REQ-PRIV-161`'s mandatory clause — "The diagnostic-bundle UI must show the user
what will be included before submission or export" — has no implementation.

The settings copy already promises the user a sharing choice the build does not
offer, and the packet's recovery clause about export failure describes behaviour
that cannot occur.

### F-09 — HIGH — The capability explanation surface is unreachable

*Lenses:* Browser, Adversarial, Testing. *Status:* CONFIRMED.

`CapabilitiesPanel` does everything `REQ-EXEC-216` and WU-01.D ask for, and no
preset contains it and no command opens a panel. `DiagnosticsPanel` is in one
preset that cannot be selected. What a user gets instead is the status bar's
"N capabilities unavailable" as plain text. On Chromium N is zero and nobody
notices; on Firefox and Safari there are real absences whose stated reasons and
remedies no user can read. The packet requires that unsupported capabilities are
"represented explicitly, not silently ignored".

### F-10 — HIGH — The refusal channel is broken three ways

*Lenses:* UX/Accessibility. *Status:* CONFIRMED.

`InteractionStore.announce` increments a sequence so that saying the same thing
twice is two announcements, and `Announcer` never passes the sequence to the DOM.
React sees identical children, leaves the text node alone, and the live region
does not fire. The second and every later refusal is silent.

The live region is rendered inside `.ag-app`, which Radix marks
`aria-hidden="true"` while a dialogue is open, so an announcement raised from the
settings dialogue is read to nobody.

There is no visual channel at all: a sighted user who runs an unavailable command
gets nothing — no toast, no status-bar line — although the status bar already
carries a pending chord and a recovery notice.

Separately, `aria-live` is mutated between polite and assertive on one
`role="status"` element, which is unreliable across screen readers.
`REQ-UX-005`, `REQ-EDIT-073`.

### F-11 — HIGH — Focus restoration fails whenever a portalled surface was used

*Lenses:* UX/Accessibility. *Status:* CONFIRMED by reading; the two scenarios are
reproducible by hand.

`ModalDialog` remembers the last element focused outside its own content. Radix's
select, popover and menu content are portalled, so they are *not* inside the
dialogue's content element: using the Theme select inside Settings records a
portalled option as the restore target. It is gone by the time the dialogue
closes, `isConnected` is false, the handler returns without preventing the
default, Radix restores to a trigger the dialogue does not have, and focus lands
on `document.body`.

The same happens when a dialogue is opened from the palette, because the palette
closes and the dialogue opens in one commit. The `isConnected` guard prevents a
crash and provides no fallback. `REQ-UX-005`, WCAG 2.4.3.

### F-12 — HIGH — The architecture rules' import matcher misses two import forms

*Lenses:* Testing. *Status:* CONFIRMED.

`importOf` and the deep-import and exports-map rules are anchored on the literal
`from`, so a side-effect import and a dynamic import are invisible to seven
rules. `apps/web/src/app.tsx` imports three cross-package specifiers in exactly
that form, so the two rules policing cross-package access skip the way this
application actually writes them. The third-party package patterns are also
anchored at both ends, so `dockview-core/dist/...` is missed. `REQ-EXEC-184`.

### F-13 — HIGH — The system colour-scheme and contrast wiring is untestable and untested

*Lenses:* Testing. *Status:* CONFIRMED.

`resolveDarkness` and `resolveContrast` are well tested against hand-built
values. The code that produces those values from the browser is tested by
nothing: jsdom's stub answers `false` to every query, and no browser test
emulates `prefers-color-scheme` or `prefers-contrast` or switches the shell into
system mode. Inverting the query in `theme-provider.tsx` leaves 748 unit tests
and 176 browser tests green. The reduced-motion arm is covered properly, which
shows the mechanism was available. `REQ-UX-070`, `REQ-EXEC-215`.

### F-14 — HIGH — The build leaks a real user path into a deployable artefact

*Lenses:* Security/Privacy. *Status:* CONFIRMED.

`apps/web/dist/sw.js.map` carries
`C:/Users/<account>/AppData/Local/Temp/<hash>/sw.js` as its only source, written
by the service-worker generator through a temporary directory. `dist/` is
ignored by git, so nothing is committed, and `dist/` is exactly what a Pages
deployment uploads. No gate looks at build output. `REQ-PRIV-161`, and the
repository's own rule against committing a real path.

### F-15 — HIGH — The reason an entry is unavailable reaches nobody outside Chromium

*Lenses:* Browser, UX/Accessibility. *Status:* CONFIRMED.

`menuItemContent` renders the label and the shortcut and drops
`unavailableReason`; the reason is carried only by `aria-description`, an ARIA
1.3 attribute that Gecko and WebKit do not implement. Radix also makes a disabled
item unfocusable, so the roving focus and the typeahead skip it and the
description is never read even in Chromium. Combined with F-01, which stops the
disabled styling rendering, the entry is neither dimmed nor explained: it simply
does nothing. The command palette does this correctly, with the reason as visible
text. `REQ-EDIT-073`, `REQ-UX-005`.

## Re-review, after the remediation

`contracts/review-gates.md` step 6 requires the affected lenses to run again.
All seven ran, read-only, against `3d4c669`, with the packet, the requirements,
this record and the rewritten evidence. Each verified its own earlier findings
against the code and looked for what the remediation itself had introduced.

Every finding of the first review is closed, with two exceptions its own lens
recorded: F-35, which is closed for the symbols it named and reopened smaller as
F-91, and F-02, whose open question about Chromium's focus ring is unchanged.

The second round found 62 further findings. Six were HIGH and none was BLOCKER
or CRITICAL.

| Lens | Findings | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | 8 | 1 HIGH |
| Code Quality / Maintainability | 10 | 2 HIGH |
| Testing / Regression | 10 | none |
| UX / Accessibility / Input | 15 | 3 HIGH |
| Security / Privacy | 7 | none |
| Browser / Platform Compatibility | 9 | 2 HIGH |
| Adversarial Agent-Quality | 9 | 1 HIGH |

Where two lenses found one defect it carries one identifier, as in the first
round: the arrangement being unreachable without a drag was raised by UX and by
Browser, and the incomplete disposition table by Code Quality, UX and the
adversarial lens. A finding is counted once for each lens that raised it, which
is why the lens counts add up to more than the findings. The table said fourteen
UX findings and ten adversarial ones until the third round recounted it from
the rows (F-219), and one Browser HIGH until the fourth recounted the Blocking
column the same way (F-278): F-115 and F-126 are both the Browser lens's.

## What the reviewers found sound

Recorded so the gate shows coverage rather than only failure. Each lens examined
and cleared: the Dockview and Radix containment rules and their mutation-proved
history; the three-layer telemetry prohibition, which `packages/diagnostics`
enforces structurally by compiling without the DOM library; the `DomainResult`
failure model and all eleven `catch` blocks; the OKLCH colour mathematics and the
contrast solver's convergence; brightness as a palette rebuild rather than a
filter; the independent editorial palettes; the layout validator's per-field
messages and its recovery reason; the diagnostic record type that makes audio
unloggable by construction; the redaction patterns across four path conventions;
the command registry's refusal of an undoable command with no inverse and its
all-or-nothing groups; the capability registry's single home for every
explanation; the shortcut edge's use of physical key codes, its modifier
suppression and its blur handling; the command palette's keyboard model, which is
the model the menus should follow; the reduced-motion policy; the determinism of
the fixtures and of the whole test suite; the absence of any skipped, focused or
weakened test in the phase's history; and the accuracy of every commit message
against its diff.

## Disposition

Remediation is recorded here as it lands, finding by finding, with the commit
that closed it. Nothing is closed on a reviewer's word alone: each fix carries a
regression test where the defect is mechanically testable, and the affected
lenses are re-run afterwards, as `contracts/review-gates.md` requires.

| Id | Disposition |
| --- | --- |
| F-01 | **Fixed.** The theme is written onto the document element as well as onto the provider's own root, so a surface portalled into the document body inherits every token. Four browser tests now read the computed background, padding and token of an open dialogue and an open menu, and the light theme's lightness inside a dialogue. Three of the four fail against the old code. |
| F-02 | **Fixed, with one question open.** The focus ring, the transition tokens and the minimal-motion guard are scoped to the theme attribute rather than to the application element, so they reach a portalled surface. A test now walks ten controls of the settings dialogue and asserts a visible ring of at least two pixels with the theme resolved at each stop. Open: on some controls Chromium draws the ring at its own width and colour although the served stylesheet sets both as longhands, and the rule is the last one the browser reports as matching. The ring is visible everywhere; its colour is not always the token. Recorded rather than left unsaid. |
| F-47 | **Fixed.** `reuseExistingServer` is off unconditionally. It was actively costing evidence: a measurement during this remediation was taken against a stale build. |
| F-03 | **Fixed.** The adapter measures; a new `geometry.ts` decides. `regionFromGeometry` reads the region from the group's rectangle against the workspace's, testing the bottom first because a bottom strip touches the left edge too, with a two-pixel tolerance for the splitter and a share threshold so a wide group is the main area however far left it starts. `proportionOf` measures a side region by width and a bottom region by height, which is the axis the user drags. `layoutFrom` is the whole read-back path with no engine types in it, so it is tested in nineteen cases without mounting anything; two of them fail against the old behaviour. The browser test that claimed to cover this asserted the layout's name and now asserts the panels' positions. |
| F-06 | **Fixed.** The validator checks `builtIn` and the layout-level `activePanelId`, and carries its proof: `isWorkspaceLayout` is a predicate, so `resolveLayout` no longer asserts what the check established. `closureProblem` gives the refusal its own answer, so "that panel is not open" is no longer indistinguishable from "that is the only panel left" — which is what made the shell announce "The panel is closed." while nothing closed. Six tests, including one for a layout that marks no panel active at all, which is allowed. |
| F-05 | **Fixed.** The workspaces the user made are kept under their own key and hydrated into the layout store on the next load, through the `userLayouts` parameter that already existed for it. Each is validated on its own, so one layout naming a panel this build does not have costs the user that layout rather than all of them. A test builds a store, saves a workspace, builds a second store over the same storage and finds it listed; it fails against the old code. |
| F-15 | **Fixed.** A menu entry renders the reason it cannot be chosen as text, which is how the command palette has always shown it, so it is part of the entry's accessible name and every assistive technology reads it. The `aria-description` attribute that carried it is removed: Gecko and WebKit do not implement it, and it sat on an element the roving focus and the typeahead both skip. |
| — | **Found while fixing F-01.** `transition-duration` on every element left `transition-property` at its initial `all`, so once the rule reached the floating surfaces a menu animated into position and a pen or touch tap landed where an entry had been a frame earlier. | — | **Found while fixing F-01.** The browser suite ran sixteen WebKit contexts against one preview server, and a menu opened by pointer intermittently failed to open. The same project passes every test with fewer workers, so the worker count is capped at four. That is a limit on the harness, not a retry and not a weakened assertion. |
| F-12 | **Fixed** in `22252ad`. The rules read the specifiers a file imports rather than matching the literal `from`, and match a package pattern against the package name alone, so side-effect, dynamic, CommonJS, stylesheet and subpath imports are all seen. Stylesheets are read too; the workspace package's own `@import` of the engine's stylesheet is named as permitted. Twelve positive controls. Proved: with three violating imports injected, the old rules reported 33 passing tests and the new ones fail four. |

The generated service worker has no source map. `tools/check-build-output.mjs` runs inside `pnpm build` and fails on this machine's own roots anywhere in the output, or on an absolute path of any machine in a map's path fields; a path is reported by file and field with its shape only. Against the leaking build it reports `sw.js.map` and nothing else. **Found with it:** `tsc` wrote declarations into the deployable `dist/`; the bundled application now compiles to `build/`. |

### The re-review's findings

The second round's findings, each with what was done. A row that says
**Tracked** is a `LOW` or a `NOTE` left open deliberately, with its owner named,
as `contracts/review-gates.md` allows; a row that says **Accepted** is one where
the reviewer's reading was considered and the current behaviour kept, with the
reason. Every `MEDIUM` and above is fixed. The third round found nineteen of
these rows claiming more than the code did; each carries its correction, marked
as the third round's, after what it first said (F-191).

| Id | Disposition |

| F-86 | **Fixed** in the second remediation round. The dock reports an arrangement, which carries only the groups and the active panel; the workspace's identity comes from the one on screen, so nothing the dock remembers can rename a workspace or be refused as another's. A browser test renames a workspace, drags a panel and reloads; it fails against the old code. **Corrected in the third round (F-191, F-217).** The browser test that proves it renames and then drags a splitter, a resize, not a panel. The arrangement takes only its identity from the screen: its groups are the caller's, validated as a layout, so a replayed one can move panels, which is what the command is for, and cannot rename or overwrite a workspace. |
| F-87 | **Fixed.** The adapter coalesces the engine's event to one report per animation frame, so a drag costs one command, one validation and one write per frame rather than per pointer move. **Corrected in the third round (F-191, F-215).** It reported up to twice a frame, and a report that provoked a change was reported again inside itself. The coalescer now reports the first change at once and at most once a frame after it, and is tested on its own. |
| F-88 | **Fixed.** `StateStorage` is guarded by the command-route rule, with `get` and `subscribe` allowed. |
| F-89 | **Fixed.** The detector reads a binding element wherever it appears and an element access with a literal name, each with a control. **Corrected in the third round (F-191, F-172).** Neither new branch had a control, and a template literal escaped both; a control file now reaches a store all three ways. |
| F-90 | **Fixed.** The workspace generator emits the stylesheet export only for a package that ships stylesheets, and the manifest rule asserts it. **Corrected in the third round (F-191, F-173).** No rule asserted it; one now reads every manifest both ways. |

## The third round, over the second remediation

`contracts/review-gates.md` step 6 again. All seven lenses ran, read-only,
against `b306f64`, with the packet, the requirements, this record and the
evidence, and were asked to verify the second round's dispositions against the
code and to find what the second remediation had introduced. Each lens numbered
its own findings from F-148, so the numbers they reported collide; they are
renumbered here, sequentially from F-148, and a defect found by more than one
lens is one finding with the lenses listed together.

| Lens | Findings | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | 12 | 2 HIGH |
| Code Quality / Maintainability | 18 | none |
| Testing / Regression | 14 | none |
| UX / Accessibility / Input | 22 | 3 HIGH |
| Security / Privacy | 15 | 2 HIGH |
| Browser / Platform Compatibility | 13 | 2 HIGH |
| Adversarial Agent-Quality | 14 | 3 HIGH |

Counted from the rows, a finding once for each lens that raised it and F-191
once for each of the seven, and the Blocking column at each row's recorded
grade. The table first gave each lens's own report, which did not reconcile
with the rows; the fourth round recounted it (F-284).

A hundred and two reported findings merge into seventy-eight: seven HIGH,
thirty-seven MEDIUM, twenty-three LOW and eleven NOTE. None was BLOCKER or
CRITICAL. The adversarial lens graded the loss of every saved workspace HIGH
rather than CRITICAL because it needs two faults at once, and said so; the
Security lens graded the same two defects MEDIUM, and the higher grade is the
one recorded. The UX lens's first HIGH is those same two defects seen from the interface,
and is merged into F-150 and F-151 below.

Most of what the round found, the second remediation had introduced: the
coalescing that made a drag cheap made a remount report into the wrong
workspace, the recovery that kept a damaged collection lost what was saved
beside it, and the chord prefix that got the palette away from Firefox's private
window put two other chords on presses the browser takes. Every finding was
verified against the code before anything changed for it.

### The third round's dispositions

As before: **Tracked** is a `LOW` or a `NOTE` left open with its owner named,
and **Accepted** is a reading considered and the behaviour kept, with the
reason. Every `HIGH` is fixed. Every `MEDIUM` is fixed except two, each accepted
in part with its reason and its owner. Every fix that is mechanically testable
carries a test that was run against the code it guards, with the defect put
back, and seen to fail. **Corrected in the fourth round (F-231, F-243).** Not
every one did: F-148's case had no test, and F-149's and F-160's tests held the
coalescer and not the dock that had the defect. Both are now tested, and the
fourth round's rows name the mutation each test was proved with (F-244).

## The fourth round, over the third remediation

`contracts/review-gates.md` step 6 once more. The seven lenses ran read-only
against `70fcf81`, with the packet, the requirements, this record and the
evidence, and were asked to verify the third round's dispositions against the
code and to find what the third remediation had introduced. Each lens numbered
its findings with its own prefix; they are numbered here from F-226, and a
defect more than one lens found is one finding with the lenses listed together.
Two of the UX lens's verdicts on third-round rows, that F-207 and F-208 were
closed in part, are recorded as findings of their own.

| Lens | Findings | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | 11 | none |
| Code Quality / Maintainability | 12 | none |
| Testing / Regression | 11 | none |
| UX / Accessibility / Input | 13 | 1 HIGH |
| Security / Privacy | 10 | 1 HIGH |
| Browser / Platform Compatibility | 7 | none |
| Adversarial Agent-Quality | 10 | 1 HIGH |

Counted from the rows, as the rounds before are: the table first gave each
lens's own report, which F-326 found did not reconcile. Seventy reported
findings and two partial closures merge into fifty-nine: two
HIGH, twenty-one MEDIUM, twenty-five LOW and eleven NOTE. None was BLOCKER or
CRITICAL. The UX and adversarial lenses found the same HIGH, the loss of what
was saved beside a partly damaged collection, from the interface and from the
store.

Most of what the round found, the third remediation had left half done or had
introduced: the recovery that kept a wholly damaged collection lost a partly
damaged one, the path rule that let an apostrophe into a name refused the slash
after a quote, and the field-name rule that stopped redacting a time signature
stopped redacting `apikey` as well. The adversarial lens also judged that F-191,
nineteen dispositions claiming more than the code did, fitted HIGH better than
the MEDIUM it was recorded at; it is corrected, and the grade stands as a
matter of record rather than of consequence. Every finding was verified against
the code before anything changed for it.

### The fourth round's dispositions

As before: **Tracked** is a `LOW` or a `NOTE` left open with its owner named,
and **Accepted** is a reading considered and the behaviour kept, with the
reason. Every `HIGH` and every `MEDIUM` is fixed. Each disposition that claims a
test names the mutation that made it fail: the defect put back in the code, or
the test run against the code at `70fcf81`, and seen to fail, then passing
again once the code was restored.

On any damage, whole or partial, its text is copied aside under `audiogubbins.workspaces.unreadable` and read back before anything is written; only when that copy is refused is the collection written beside the damaged text, and the copy written beside it is read on any damage. Store tests save, delete and reload with a wholly and a partly damaged file, and with the set-aside refused. Proof: the six store tests fail against the store at `70fcf81`. **Corrected in the fifth round (F-286).** A refused collection write still deleted the copy beside it; the copy goes now only after a write that was kept. **Corrected in the sixth round (F-341).** The removal answered for the whole write, so a refused layout key kept a copy the collection had made stale. ## The fifth round, over the fourth remediation

`contracts/review-gates.md` step 6 again. The seven lenses ran read-only
against `56c4a4c`, with the packet, the requirements, this record, the evidence
and the resume note, and were asked to verify the fourth round's dispositions,
its thirty-five corrections and its counts against the code, and to find what
the fourth remediation had introduced. Numbered from F-285, a defect found by
more than one lens being one finding with the lenses listed together. One
Browser finding held two defects, and is two findings here.

| Lens | Findings | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | 9 | none |
| Code Quality / Maintainability | 13 | none |
| Testing / Regression | 8 | none |
| UX / Accessibility / Input | 11 | none |
| Security / Privacy | 13 | 2 HIGH |
| Browser / Platform Compatibility | 5 | none |
| Adversarial Agent-Quality | 11 | 1 HIGH |

Counted from the rows, a finding once for each lens that raised it, and the
Blocking column at each row's recorded grade. Security's sixth finding named
two defects, the copy's removal and its damaged text, and counts on both rows,
F-286 and F-288, which is why the table sums to seventy. Sixty-eight reported
findings merge into fifty-five: two HIGH, eleven MEDIUM, thirty-one LOW and eleven NOTE.
None was BLOCKER or CRITICAL.

Both HIGHs are the kind the rounds before kept finding: a rule written for the
form a test used, a name with a path around it, and not for the form a browser
produces, a name alone; and a recovery that protected against one refusal and
lost the text to the next. Every finding was verified against the code before
anything changed for it.

against `929f8e9`, with the packet, the requirements, this record, the evidence
and the resume note, and were asked to verify the fifth round's dispositions,
its twelve corrections and its counts against the code, and to find what the
fifth remediation had introduced. Numbered from F-340, a defect found by more
than one lens being one finding with the lenses listed together.

Counted from the rows, a finding once for each lens that raised it, and the

of them a note the Code Quality lens left unnumbered, and the regrade of F-305
the Adversarial lens asked for, merge into forty-six: one HIGH, eight MEDIUM,
twenty-nine LOW and eight NOTE. None was BLOCKER or CRITICAL. The table sums to
sixty-seven: three findings named two defects each and count on both rows, and
the regrade counts for the two lenses that raised it.

### The sixth round's dispositions

As before, and each test named with the mutation it was proved with: the defect

| F-340 | **Fixed.** `userFileNamesIn` in `path-finding.ts` reads a name back from its extension to the first thing no name holds: the start of the text or of its line, a double quote, an angle bracket, a bar or a backtick, a label or a clause ended by a colon or a semicolon, or the end of the name before it. Every word on the way is taken, whatever it looks like: the words of the sentence before a name are the cost of never leaving a part of it behind, the trade the path rules make. A name in quotes starts after the quote that closes straight after it, and a bracket is part of a name. Proof: thirteen forms, asserted whole, fail against the diagnostics modules at `929f8e9`. **Corrected in the eighth round (F-513).** "Never leaving a part of it behind" was untrue: a name holding a double quote and a quoted word before a possessive were left (F-428). |

It is removed only once it was readable or is set aside, in a write after one that kept the collection's own key: `StateStorage.save` answers with the keys it refused. Proof: a three-session test fails with the old reading of a copy beside a whole collection, and a test refusing the layout key fails with the old answer for the whole part. **Corrected in the seventh round (F-389, F-446).** A copy beside a collection this build reads whole was still removed in the first write, unread; it is set aside now, and removed only in a later write. ## The seventh round, over the sixth remediation

`contracts/review-gates.md` step 6 again. The seven lenses ran read-only
against `38ee4f1`, with the packet, the requirements, this record, the evidence
and the resume note, and were asked to verify the sixth round's dispositions,
its twenty-six corrections and its counts against the code, and to find what
the sixth remediation had introduced. Numbered from F-386, a defect found by
more than one lens being one finding with the lenses listed together.

| Lens | Findings | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | 10 | 1 HIGH |
| Code Quality / Maintainability | 16 | none |
| Testing / Regression | 10 | none |
| UX / Accessibility / Input | 13 | 1 HIGH |
| Security / Privacy | 11 | 1 HIGH |
| Browser / Platform Compatibility | 11 | 1 HIGH |
| Adversarial Agent-Quality | 12 | 1 HIGH |

Counted from the rows, a finding once for each lens that raised it, and the
Blocking column at each row's recorded grade. Eighty reported findings merge
into sixty, and one more was found while they were fixed (F-399): two HIGH,
twelve MEDIUM, thirty-nine LOW and eight NOTE, sixty-one in all. None was
BLOCKER or CRITICAL. The table sums to eighty-three: three reported findings
named two defects each and count on both rows, the Architecture lens's first
and the UX lens's first on F-386 and F-388, and the Testing lens's fourth on
F-418 and F-432. F-399 counts on no row, since no lens reported it.

The HIGHs are F-386, found by four lenses: a stored shortcut profile was read
at every start on a keyboard layout not known yet, and a binding made on
another layout was read as one the browser takes, dropped, and written away;
and F-387, a regression the sixth round's F-345 brought, which kept a secret
whole when its value began with a word and `=` or `:`. Every finding was
verified against the code before anything changed for it; F-399 was found by
a browser probe while F-424 was being fixed.

## The eighth round, over the seventh remediation

`contracts/review-gates.md` step 6 again. The seven lenses ran read-only
against `ad3a5c5`, with the packet, the requirements, this record, the evidence
and the resume note, and were asked to verify the seventh round's dispositions,
its twenty-nine corrections and its counts against the code, and to find what
the seventh remediation had introduced. Numbered from F-447, a defect found by
more than one lens being one finding with the lenses listed together. Each
lens's report and the proof log of this round were kept outside the tree as
they were written, and are the source of every count and proof below.

| Lens | Findings | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | 15 | none |
| Code Quality / Maintainability | 21 | none |
| Testing / Regression | 9 | none |
| UX / Accessibility / Input | 12 | none |
| Security / Privacy | 11 | 1 HIGH |
| Browser / Platform Compatibility | 10 | none |
| Adversarial Agent-Quality | 11 | none |

Counted from the reports, a finding once for each lens that raised it, at the
grade it was reported at. Eighty-nine reported findings merge into seventy-one:
one HIGH, twelve MEDIUM, forty LOW and eighteen NOTE. None was BLOCKER or
CRITICAL. The merges are these, the first named lens's grade kept where they
differ:

- F-448: Architecture's second, UX's second, Adversarial's first and Browser's fifth.
- F-449: Architecture's third, Browser's first and Testing's first.
- F-450: Architecture's first and UX's tenth.
- F-459: Adversarial's second and Browser's tenth.
- F-461: Architecture's fifth and Code Quality's second.
- F-462: Architecture's sixth and Code Quality's fourteenth.
- F-463: Architecture's seventh, UX's eleventh and Code Quality's seventeenth.
- F-464: Architecture's eighth and Code Quality's eighth.
- F-465: Architecture's ninth and Code Quality's tenth.
- F-470: Architecture's fourteenth and UX's fifth.
- F-474: Code Quality's fourth and Adversarial's sixth.
- F-489: Testing's fifth and Adversarial's fifth.
- F-493: Testing's ninth and Browser's ninth.
- F-497: UX's seventh and Adversarial's seventh.

The HIGH is F-447: a secret, or the credentials in an address, written straight
after a dot that follows a character outside a name was kept whole,
`users[0].password=hunter2` and `Retrying (2/3)...postgres://admin:hunter2@host`
among them, a regression the seventh round's F-427 brought. Every finding was
verified against the code before anything changed for it; the dock's read-back
after a resize (F-449) was first reproduced in a browser by the test that now
holds it.

## The ninth round, over the eighth remediation

`contracts/review-gates.md` step 6 again. The seven lenses ran read-only
against `b45d0ce`, with the packet, the requirements, this record, the evidence
and the resume note, and were asked to verify the eighth round's dispositions,
its thirty-six corrections and its counts against the code, and to find what
the eighth remediation had introduced. Numbered from F-518, a defect found by
more than one lens being one finding with the lenses listed together. Each
lens's report and the proof log of this round were kept outside the tree as
they were written, and are the source of every count and proof below.

## The tenth round, over the ninth remediation

`contracts/review-gates.md` step 6 again. The seven lenses ran read-only
against `cb375a5`, with the packet, the requirements, this record, the evidence
and the resume note, and were asked to verify the ninth round's dispositions,
its thirty-seven corrections and its counts against the code, and to find what
the ninth remediation had introduced. Numbered from F-566, a defect found by
more than one lens being one finding with the lenses listed together. Each
lens's report and the proof log of this round were kept outside the tree as
they were written, and are the source of every count and proof below.

| Lens | Findings | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | 9 | none |
| Code Quality / Maintainability | 11 | none |
| Testing / Regression | 10 | none |
| UX / Accessibility / Input | 15 | none |
| Security / Privacy | 11 | none |
| Browser / Platform Compatibility | 10 | none |
| Adversarial Agent-Quality | 10 | none |

Counted from the reports, a finding once for each lens that raised it, at the
grade it was reported at. Seventy-six reported findings merge into sixty-four:
three HIGH, thirteen MEDIUM, twenty-one LOW and twenty-seven NOTE. None was
BLOCKER or CRITICAL. The merges are these, the first named lens's grade kept
where they differ:

- F-568: Browser's second and Testing's first.
- F-569: UX's second, Browser's third, Adversarial's first and Adversarial's eighth.
- F-579: Browser's fourth and UX's ninth.
- F-580: Adversarial's second, Code Quality's eleventh and Architecture's fifth.

- F-586: Architecture's sixth and Adversarial's fourth.

- F-597: Code Quality's tenth and Testing's seventh.

Every finding was verified against the code before anything changed for it:
the redaction findings by a probe run over the reported inputs, the contrast
of the highlighted entry by solving the tokens the themes publish, the sizes
by measuring with the rules' own `logicalLines`, and the rest by reading.
Three premises could not be run here and are said with their dispositions:
what a macOS browser reports for a Command press made with Shift or Option
(F-568), what the ⌘ layer does on an engine that does not apply it (F-624),
and what a Chromebook's own system takes (F-620).

One of this round's own fixes had a defect a new test caught while it was
being written: the tri-state read a character no US layout types unshifted,
`+` on a German layout, as an unresolved disagreement. It is fixed, and
"is told nothing by a Command press on a key both layers type alike" holds it.

### The tenth round's dispositions

As before, each test named with the mutation it was proved with: the defect put
back, or the test run against the code before the fix, and seen to fail, then
passing with the code restored. Each group of mutations carries a control that
has to leave its test passing, and every control now writes to a production
file the group itself mutates (F-601). A defect run against a test that cannot
see it is a gap, reported as one, and is no longer counted as a control
(F-602). A row with no behaviour to prove says so.

## The eleventh round, over the tenth remediation

`contracts/review-gates.md` step 6 again. The seven lenses ran read-only
against `9f9e2ac`, with the packet, the requirements, this record, the evidence
and the resume note, and were asked to verify the tenth round's dispositions,
its sixteen corrections and its counts against the code, and to find what the
tenth remediation had introduced. Numbered from F-630, a defect found by more
than one lens being one finding with the lenses listed together. Each lens's
report and the proof log of this round were kept outside the tree as they were
written, and are the source of every count and proof below.

**Corrected in the nineteenth round (F-1027).** The tenth round made seventeen
corrections that carry its marker, not sixteen. The seventeenth, its correction
to the ninth round's preamble (F-626), was written with the marker broken across
two lines of this record, and every count taken line by line missed it, the
lenses' among them; the tenth round's two paragraphs of prose corrections,
F-628's and F-626's, carry no marker and are in no count. Since the nineteenth
round a rule counts every marker over the record's text with its whitespace run
together, and the evidence and the resume note give the tenth round seventeen.

F-651 is the one merge where the grade is not the first lens's by

Every finding was verified against the code before anything changed for it: the
quadratic redaction by measuring the two patterns over the same inputs, the
palette's pointer route by writing the browser test and watching it fail on
WebKit before anything was changed, the sizes by measuring with the rules' own
`logicalLines`, and the rest by reading. Premises that could not be run here
are said with their own dispositions, each beginning "Premise not run:", and
the list is taken from the "Could not settle without running" section of each
kept lens report rather than from memory: F-641 (which engines deliver
Control+Shift+B and Control+Shift+D to the page), F-684 (what an Android tablet
with a keyboard and a Chromebook deliver), F-671 (whether a screen reader
speaks an arrow glyph at its default verbosity) and F-690 (which of Command
with the arrow keys macOS delivers to the page).

One of this round's own fixes had a defect a new test caught while it was being
written: the growth case over a line of `a:` pairs measured at a size where the
fixed form finishes in a fraction of a millisecond, so its ratio was noise and
it failed once under the load of the full suite. It measures one hundred
thousand pairs now, which is what the harness's own doc asks for.

### The eleventh round's dispositions

As before, each test named with the mutation it was proved with: the defect put
back, or the test run against the code before the fix, and seen to fail, then
passing with the code restored. Each group of mutations carries a control that
has to leave its test passing, and the architecture group now carries one for
each path root it writes into rather than one for the three (F-667). A defect
run against a test that cannot see it is a gap, reported as one; this round
runs one. A row with no behaviour to prove says so.

| Id | Disposition |

| F-630 | **Fixed.** The drive-relative root looks ahead over a first segment that holds no colon, which no Windows segment may, so the scan ends at the first one: 800 kB of `a:` pairs went from nearly two minutes to under a millisecond. The reproduction note is bounded where it is read, and the field declares the same bound rather than cutting what the reader has written. The doc now describes the rule the code has. Proof: the colon back inside the first segment fails "reads a line of letter-and-colon pairs once, not once a pair"; the note unbounded fails "carries a reproduction note no longer than any anyone writes"; the field without its bound fails "stops the reader at the bound what reads the value has". **Corrected in the twelfth round (F-714).** "Under a millisecond" is a figure the code cannot produce. Timed over the rebuilt pattern alone, 800 kB of those pairs takes about 7 ms, growing cleanly with the length, and `redactText` runs every other rule over the same text besides. What the case asserts, and what the fix is for, is that doubling the length costs less than three times the time. **Corrected in the thirteenth round (F-796).** The figure above was measured while the eleventh round was reviewed and is in no proof log, and the row does not say where it came from, which is what F-736 was raised for. It is the Security lens's own probe of the rebuilt pattern over 100 kB to 800 kB of letter-and-colon pairs, on the machine this phase was written on, recorded in that lens's round-12 report. What the suite holds is the growth property, not the figure. |

## The twelfth round, over the eleventh remediation

`contracts/review-gates.md` step 6 again. The seven lenses ran read-only
against `7d255f6`, with the packet, the requirements, this record, the evidence
and the resume note, and were asked to verify the eleventh round's
dispositions, its thirty-five corrections and its counts against the code, and
to find what the eleventh remediation had introduced. Numbered from F-695, a
defect found by more than one lens being one finding with the lenses listed
together. Each lens's report and the proof log of this round were kept outside
the tree as they were written, and are the source of every count and proof
below.

| Lens | Findings | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | 6 | none |
| Code Quality / Maintainability | 11 | none |
| Testing / Regression | 8 | none |
| UX / Accessibility / Input | 11 | 1 HIGH |
| Security / Privacy | 6 | none |
| Browser / Platform Compatibility | 8 | none |
| Adversarial Agent-Quality | 10 | none |

Counted from the reports, a finding once for each lens that raised it, at the
grade it was reported at. Sixty reported findings merge into fifty-two: one
HIGH, eight MEDIUM, fifteen LOW and twenty-eight NOTE. None was BLOCKER or
CRITICAL. Two more were found while fixing them — F-747 and F-748, both LOW,
both from writing the test F-732 asks for — so the table below holds fifty-four
rows, F-695 to F-748: one HIGH, eight MEDIUM, seventeen LOW and twenty-eight
NOTE. The merges are these, the first named lens's grade kept where they
differ:

- F-695: UX's first and Browser's first.
- F-697: Security's first, Testing's second and Adversarial's tenth.
- F-699: Browser's second and UX's fifth.
- F-704: Code Quality's first, Architecture's second and Code Quality's ninth.
- F-706: Architecture's third and Adversarial's third.
- F-717: Browser's fifth and Testing's seventh.

One HIGH, and it is the eleventh round's own fix for F-638 reached by another
route: the note that ends the Command wait named a key by sort order, which on
Apple hardware is the comma, and no reading of a Command press is taken from a
press of the key that types one. On AZERTY the settings shortcut could then
never be placed at all. Two merges keep the higher grade against the first
named lens by position: F-699, where Browser's MEDIUM stands over UX's LOW
because it is the class F-631 was graded HIGH for, narrowed to pen users on the
engine the defect was measured on; and F-717, where Browser's LOW stands over
Testing's NOTE.

**Corrected in the thirteenth round (F-793).** Three merges do, not two. By the
convention the eleventh round wrote down — the first lens by position in the
table above — F-704 is a third: Code Quality's LOW is kept over Architecture's
NOTE, and Architecture is first in that table. The grade kept is the right one
in each of the three; it is the count of exceptions that was short, and the
exceptions are listed precisely so that a reader can check them.

Every finding was verified against the code before anything changed for it: the

hand and then writing the sweep that reads it from the rendered note, the

between them, the contrast requirement by running the solver over every accent
and brightness step, and the rest by reading. Where a claim needed a number, it
was measured rather than estimated.

**Corrected in the thirteenth round (F-795).** "And the rest by reading"
disagrees with the round's own Verification column, which names a run for at

### The twelfth round's dispositions

As before, each test named with the mutation it was proved with: the defect put
back, or the test run against the code before the fix, and seen to fail, then
passing with the code restored. Each group of mutations carries a control that
has to leave its test passing, written into a production file the group
mutates. A row with no behaviour to prove says so.

| Id | Disposition |
| --- | --- |
| F-695 | **Fixed.** The key the note names is asked of the layout, by the three conditions `commandLayerOf` reads a press by: a letter key, typing a letter, which a US layout types somewhere else. One qualifying press settles the reading for every waiting default at once, so which shortcut waits decides nothing about which key ends the wait, and a default's own character need not sit on a key that can end it. Where the layout has shown no such key, the note says so and says what would make one known, rather than naming a key: that is the second sentence the old note had no room for. `WaitingDefault` carries whether a default waits for the layer and no longer which characters, and `DefaultPlacement` carries a set, because every reader but the defect used the list as a boolean. Proof: each of the three conditions dropped in turn fails "is a letter key typing a letter that a US layout types somewhere else"; the note naming a key of the layout's own fails "names a key a Command press is read from, on every layout a default waits on", which reads the character out of the rendered note on every fixture layout and takes it back through `commandLayerOf` both ways; the second sentence replaced by the old naming fails "says that no key of the reader can show it, where the layout has shown none". **Corrected in the thirteenth round (F-749).** The key the note names is read and is not delivered. `settlesCommandLayer` filtered for whether a press could be read and never for whether it arrives, so on AZERTY it named the key that quits the browser under Command and on Dvorak the key that opens a window. The layout now answers every such key and the settings take the first the platform leaves alone under either reading; on AZERTY there is none, and the note says so. **Corrected in the fourteenth round (F-815).** Two titles in the Proof were renamed in the thirteenth round, which the correction above does not say. The tests are `is each letter key typing a letter that a US layout types somewhere else` and `names a key a Command press is read from and the page receives, on every layout a default waits on`. |

The false clause in the block's own comment, that a select option never takes focus, is corrected. Proof: the select list struck from the block fails "rings the entry the keyboard is on, in a menu, a select list and the palette", and so does the menu entry struck from it; the focus-ring token set to zero still fails it. |

## The thirteenth round, over the twelfth remediation

`contracts/review-gates.md` step 6 again. The seven lenses ran read-only
against `7be9b80`, with the packet, the requirements, this record, the evidence
and the resume note, and were asked to verify the twelfth round's dispositions,
its thirty-three corrections and its counts against the code, and to find what
the twelfth remediation had introduced. Numbered from F-749, a defect found by
more than one lens being one finding with the lenses listed together. Each
lens's report and the proof log of this round were kept outside the tree as
they were written, and are the source of every count and proof below.

| Lens | Findings | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | 8 | none |
| Code Quality / Maintainability | 12 | none |
| Testing / Regression | 9 | none |
| UX / Accessibility / Input | 7 | 1 HIGH |
| Security / Privacy | 4 | none |
| Browser / Platform Compatibility | 9 | none |
| Adversarial Agent-Quality | 12 | none |

Counted from the reports, a finding once for each lens that raised it, at the
grade it was reported at. Sixty-one reported findings merge into forty-eight:
one HIGH, three MEDIUM, twenty LOW and twenty-four NOTE. None was BLOCKER or
CRITICAL. One more was found while verifying the baseline — F-797, LOW — so the
table below holds forty-nine rows, F-749 to F-797: one HIGH, three MEDIUM,
twenty-one LOW and twenty-four NOTE. The merges are these, twelve of them,
saving thirteen rows, the first named lens's grade kept where they differ:

- F-752: Adversarial's first and Testing's second.
- F-753: Architecture's first and Code Quality's fourth.
- F-755: Architecture's fourth and Adversarial's eleventh.
- F-756: Architecture's seventh and Code Quality's second.
- F-760: Code Quality's sixth and Security's fourth.
- F-761: Testing's first, Adversarial's second and Adversarial's eighth.
- F-763: Testing's fourth and Browser's second.
- F-764: UX's third and Browser's fourth.
- F-770: Testing's fifth and Adversarial's fourth.
- F-771: Testing's ninth and Adversarial's third.
- F-772: Security's third and Adversarial's fifth.
- F-782: Testing's sixth and Adversarial's tenth.

Five merges keep the higher grade against the first named lens by position in
the table above: F-752, where Adversarial's MEDIUM stands over Testing's LOW
because the row it is about was raised in the twelfth round against exactly
this shape and closed without the fix being made; F-761, where Testing's LOW
stands over Adversarial's NOTE for the third of its three rows; F-770 and
F-771, where Adversarial's LOW stands over Testing's NOTE; and F-772, where
Adversarial's LOW stands over Security's NOTE. The grade kept is the higher one
in each.

**Corrected in the fourteenth round (F-839).** Four do, not five. F-761 keeps
Testing's LOW, and Testing is first in that merge by table position, so it is
the ordinary case; and F-752 is named above with Adversarial first, out of table
order, which by this preamble's own rule would make it no exception either. By
table order it is Testing's LOW and Adversarial's MEDIUM, kept higher: F-752,
F-770, F-771 and F-772 are the four.

One HIGH, and it is the twelfth round's own fix for F-695 reached by another
route. That round stopped the note naming a key no reading is taken from, and
named instead the first key a reading *can* be taken from, which on AZERTY is
the key that quits the browser under Command and on Dvorak the key that opens a
window. The reader who follows the note loses the page and settles nothing.
AZERTY is the layout F-695 was graded HIGH for, and there this one sentence is
the whole remedy offered.

Two verdicts the lenses disagreed on were settled by reading before anything
was written down. F-739 does not hold: `assembleBundle` rebuilds every
capability summary from `key`, `available` and `reason`, so the third state the
fix added never reaches the exported report, and the fix and its test are both
over the function that builds the input. The proof log's Vitest split is wrong:
the block holds eight controls and twenty-two defects, not seven and
twenty-three.

Every finding was verified against the code before anything changed for it: the
key the note names by tracing both fixture layouts through `commandLayerOf` and
the reservation table by hand, the clipped chrome by driving the page to three
phone widths and reading the banner's right edge against the page's, the stray
build output by running the cruise with it present and again with it gone, the
forward-slash rewrite and the repository root by running each rule's own globs
over the tree, and the rest by reading. Where a claim needed a number, it was
measured rather than estimated: the banner's right edge is 409 pixels on a
320-pixel page, and the cruise reports 274 modules with the development
server's output present against 271 without it.

**Corrected in the fourteenth round (F-840).** "And the rest by reading"
disagrees with the round's own Verification column, which names a run for at
least ten more rows, as F-795 found of the round before; and of the two verdicts
the preamble says the lenses disagreed on, no lens disagreed on the Vitest
split, which was settled by a script counting the log's own entries rather than
by reading. Each row's Verification column is what stands.

One finding was found while verifying the baseline rather than by a lens. The
working tree was not clean at `7be9b80`: `apps/web/dev-dist/` held three files
the development server's service-worker plugin writes, that directory is in
neither `.gitignore` nor the list of what a build writes, and the cruise reads
`apps/`, so running the development server made the architecture gate fail on
three orphan modules. It is F-797.

### The thirteenth round's dispositions

As before, each test named with the mutation it was proved with: the defect put
back, or the test run against the code before the fix, and seen to fail, then
passing with the code restored. Each group of mutations carries a control that
has to leave its test passing, written into a production file the group
mutates. A row with no behaviour to prove says so.

**Corrected in the fourteenth round (F-846).** The convention is wider than it
was kept. The architecture group's three controls all ran one test, two of them
written into test files, and four of the tests that group mutated had no control
at all.

| Id | Disposition |
| --- | --- |
| F-749 | **Fixed.** `settlesCommandLayer` is now `commandLayerKeys`, which answers every key a reading can be taken from as a code and the character it types, in the characters' own order, and says in its doc that whether such a press ever arrives is not that package's to answer. The settings, which already import the command package, take the first key the platform leaves alone under **both** readings of the layout: which of the two the system reads is the very thing the press would settle, so there is no safe key while both are open. On Dvorak that is `c`, on the key a US keyboard types `i` on. On AZERTY it is none — the layout moves four letters, and each is read either as the key that quits the browser or as the key that closes the tab — so the note says so and points at the table below it, where a binding can be set by hand. The sweep asserts that whatever key is named is both read and delivered. Proof: the first readable key named whatever the platform does fails "names a key a Command press is read from and the page receives, on every layout a default waits on"; reading one layer alone fails it too; the layout answering one key rather than all of them fails "answers all of them, in the characters they type, so a caller can pass one over"; and the no-key sentence removed fails "says no key can be asked for, where the platform takes every one the layout offers" |
| F-750 | **Fixed** by a leaf package, `@audiogubbins/text`, holding the rules a sentence shown to a reader is held to: the characters a reader sees, the quoting of a stored or imported value, the cut at the last word that fits and the cut at a whole sentence. Its entry point offers those four and not the pieces they are built from, so a caller wanting a fifth cut reads one of these rather than assembling another. Diagnostics owns logging, redaction and bundles again, in all four descriptions. The quoting bound moves its cut back to a whole character rather than out of half a surrogate pair alone, so the cost F-738 accepted is no longer paid. `packages/input` depends on it and on nothing else, which `ADR-0017` forbade: `ADR-0018` records the amendment and names the clause it changes, ADR-0017 names the amendment on the row it changes, and the cruiser rule that keeps the input package a leaf names the one package it may reach. Proof: the quoting rule guarding a surrogate pair alone fails "never leaves a letter without the mark a reader sees on it"; the cut taken at the bound wherever it falls fails "leaves out a character the bound falls inside"; the segmenter's fallback removed fails "reads code points instead, rather than failing to load at all" **Corrected in the fourteenth round (F-801, F-822, F-833).** Three claims did not hold. The architecture rules did not keep the text package a leaf or free of the browser (F-801); ADR-0017 names the amendment on a row of its own, not on the clause it changes (F-822); and "the cost F-738 accepted is no longer paid" held only where the browser segments (F-833). The fourteenth round fixes all three, and gives the package two more rules (F-813). **Corrected in the fifteenth round (F-869).** Four claims did not hold, not three. The fourth is the fallback proof: taking the segmenter's fallback away failed its test only under the thirteenth round's filter, which ran that test alone, and could not fail in the full suite (F-802). The fourteenth round's two mutations, each running the whole file, replace it. |
| F-751 | **Fixed.** The shell's one column is `minmax(0, 1fr)`, so the track can be narrower than what is in it; the menu bar wraps rather than running off the page; and the product name gives last, with a minimum of zero and an ellipsis. ## The fourteenth round, over the thirteenth remediation

`contracts/review-gates.md` step 6 again. The seven lenses ran read-only
against `82e40d4`, with the packet, the requirements, this record, the evidence
and the resume note, and were asked to verify the thirteenth round's
dispositions, its thirty-four corrections and its counts against the code, and
to find what the thirteenth remediation had introduced. Numbered from F-798, a
defect found by more than one lens being one finding with the lenses listed
together. Each lens's report and the proof log of this round were kept outside
the tree as they were written, and are the source of every count and proof
below.

| Lens | Findings | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | 8 | none |
| Code Quality / Maintainability | 11 | none |
| Testing / Regression | 13 | none |
| UX / Accessibility / Input | 5 | none |
| Security / Privacy | 4 | none |
| Browser / Platform Compatibility | 10 | none |
| Adversarial Agent-Quality | 15 | none |

Counted from the reports, a finding once for each lens that raised it, at the
grade it was reported at. Sixty-six reported findings — six MEDIUM, twenty-three
LOW and thirty-seven NOTE, none BLOCKER, CRITICAL or HIGH — merge into fifty:
five MEDIUM, seventeen LOW and twenty-eight NOTE. One more was found while
fixing them — F-848, LOW — so the table below holds fifty-one rows, F-798 to
F-848: five MEDIUM, eighteen LOW and twenty-eight NOTE. The merges are these,
eleven of them, saving sixteen rows, each with its lenses in the order of the
table above:

- F-798: Testing's first, Security's first and Adversarial's first.
- F-799: UX's first and Browser's fourth.
- F-800: Testing's third, UX's fourth and Browser's ninth.
- F-803: Code Quality's second, Testing's sixth and Browser's first.
- F-804: Code Quality's first and Security's third.
- F-805: Architecture's seventh, Code Quality's third, Testing's eighth and
  Adversarial's fifteenth.

- F-808: Testing's thirteenth and Adversarial's second.
- F-809: UX's second and Browser's fifth.
- F-820: Code Quality's sixth and Testing's ninth.

Each merge keeps the highest grade any of its lenses gave it. Two of them keep a
grade higher than the first lens's by position in the table above, and a script
over the reports' own headings found them rather than a count typed here: F-805,
where Code Quality's LOW stands over Architecture's NOTE, and F-808, where
Adversarial's LOW stands over Testing's NOTE. In the other nine the first lens
gave the grade kept.

No finding is BLOCKER, CRITICAL or HIGH. The five MEDIUMs are all about the
thirteenth round's own remedies. F-798 is the third round running in which a
row raised for citing a test that exists nowhere was closed by citing two
more; F-799 is the thirteenth round's own fix for a notice over a dialogue,
which made room by shrinking the dialogue under the reader; F-800 is the test
written for the clipped shell, which read the wrong element; F-801 is the new
text package, which the architecture rules its decision record names did not
read; and F-802 is a proof that held only under the harness's filter.

Every finding was verified against the code before anything changed for it,
and each row's Verification column says how; that column is what stands, and
this sentence does not summarise it. Three owner decisions were taken during
the round and are recorded with the rows they decide: a bare `seed=` is
redacted (F-817); a rule reads every test title a disposition names against the
titles a run reports (F-798); and the reservation rows that no engine's own

### The fourteenth round's dispositions

As before, each test named with the mutation it was proved with: the defect put
back, or the test run against the code before the fix, and seen to fail, then
passing with the code restored. What changed in how that is run: each Vitest
mutation runs the whole test file that holds its test, not the one test alone,
and counts as caught only where the named test is among the failures, not where
anything failed; a browser mutation likewise. Each group carries at least one
control — a reworded comment in a file the group mutates, run against the whole
file its defects are run against — and the convention is stated here as it is
kept, not wider. A row with no behaviour to prove says so.

**Corrected in the fifteenth round (F-858).** The convention is stated wider
than it was kept. The recorder group's control changed an attribute in code, not
a comment; the command group's one control ran one of the two test files its
defects ran; the menu mutation's file had no control; and the browser harness
ran each mutation's test by its title on one project, not the whole spec file.

## The fifteenth round, over the fourteenth remediation

`contracts/review-gates.md` step 6 again. The seven lenses ran read-only
against `6f21d56`, with the packet, the requirements, this record, the evidence
and the resume note, and were asked to verify the fourteenth round's
dispositions, its fifty-eight corrections and its counts against the code, and
to find what the fourteenth remediation had introduced. Numbered from F-849, a
defect found by more than one lens being one finding with the lenses listed
together. Each lens's report and the proof log of this round were kept outside
the tree as they were written, and are the source of every count and proof
below.

| Lens | Findings | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | 6 | none |
| Code Quality / Maintainability | 12 | none |
| Testing / Regression | 9 | none |
| UX / Accessibility / Input | 6 | none |
| Security / Privacy | 6 | none |
| Browser / Platform Compatibility | 8 | none |
| Adversarial Agent-Quality | 10 | none |

Counted from the reports, a finding once for each lens that raised it, at the
grade it was reported at. Fifty-seven reported findings — six MEDIUM,
twenty-two LOW and twenty-nine NOTE, none BLOCKER, CRITICAL or HIGH — merge
into forty-four: four MEDIUM, seventeen LOW and twenty-three NOTE. One more
was found while proving them — F-893, MEDIUM — so the table below holds
forty-five rows, F-849 to F-893: five MEDIUM, seventeen LOW and twenty-three
NOTE. The merges are these, ten of them, saving thirteen rows, each with its
lenses in the order of the table above:

- F-849: Testing's first and Adversarial's first.
- F-850: Testing's third, UX's second and Security's first.
- F-853: Code Quality's first and Adversarial's second.
- F-854: Testing's second and Browser's second.
- F-855: Architecture's third, Code Quality's third and Adversarial's third.
- F-856: Code Quality's second and Browser's fifth.
- F-857: Architecture's sixth, Code Quality's fourth and Testing's eighth.
- F-858: Testing's fifth and Adversarial's sixth.
- F-870: Testing's sixth and Security's fifth.
- F-871: Architecture's fourth and Code Quality's sixth.

Each merge keeps the highest grade any of its lenses gave it. Two of them keep
a grade higher than the first lens's by position in the table above, and a
script over the reports' own headings found them rather than a count typed
here: F-850, where UX's and Security's MEDIUM stand over Testing's LOW, and
F-857, where Code Quality's LOW stands over Architecture's NOTE. In the other
eight the first lens gave the grade kept.

No finding is BLOCKER, CRITICAL or HIGH. Four of the five MEDIUMs are each about
a fourteenth-round remedy. F-849 is the title rule written for F-798, which read
a title only after the words it knew and so passed nine rows quoting the start
of a title; F-850 is the count in characters written for F-813, which gave up
the length bound the profile-name check was written for; F-851 is the notice
placed beside the reader's focus over a dialogue, which the dialogue itself
holding focus squeezed to a sliver; and F-852 is the removal of the zoom and
address-bar rows, which left a binding free to take them from a reader. The
fifth, F-893, is about this round's own remedy for F-851: the line it put in the
dialogue's flow was out of sight whenever the reader's focus was on a control
near the top of a dialogue that scrolls. It is graded as F-851 is, a refusal a
sighted reader is not shown.

Every finding was verified against the code before anything changed for it,
and each row's Verification column says how; that column is what stands, and
this sentence does not summarise it. Three owner decisions were taken during
the round and are recorded with the rows they decide: a press a reader relies on
the browser for — the zoom keys, the ways into the address bar and F11 — is
refused with a reason that says so, as a third kind of reservation row
(F-852); a notice raised while a dialogue is open is a line in the
dialogue's own flow, above its actions, not an overlay (F-851); and every
dialogue is a title, a part that scrolls and a footer that does not, which
holds the refusal line and the actions and takes at most 40dvh, so the
refusal is in sight wherever the reader is (F-893).

**Corrected in the sixteenth round (F-894, F-897).** The footer did not keep the
refusal in sight wherever the reader is: past 40dvh it scrolled inside itself,
and focus on an action scrolled the start of a long refusal out of it (F-897),
and on a short page, at its cap, it left the part that scrolls about one row
(F-894). Since the sixteenth round, at the owner's decision, the footer has no
cap and never scrolls on its own, the part that scrolls keeps room for one
control, and the dialogue itself scrolls as the last resort.

**Corrected in the seventeenth round (F-940).** The part that scrolls did not
keep room for one control of every kind: its content box at the floor was one
control of the density's height and its ring, 40 pixels in comfortable density,
while a control drawn for a finger under a coarse pointer is 44 pixels, and the
text field was drawn at 42 in comfortable density with a mouse too. Since the
seventeenth round the floor is set from the touch target where a finger is among
the inputs, and, at the owner's decision, the text field is drawn at the
density's control height.

One finding was numbered from the round's own work. Proving F-851 in a browser,
the line's scroll into view taken away passed the whole spec file, and a probe
on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit then found the line out of sight with focus near
the top of a dialogue that scrolls; that is F-893. Two more things the round
found are written where they belong. The rule written for F-860 was run over the
commits that ended the tenth to the fourteenth rounds, and found a third change
the evidence's lines had missed, the return type of `previewRedaction` in the
twelfth round; it is in F-860's row. Reading every quoted string in the
dispositions for F-849 found twelve more titles the widened grammar still read
nowhere, one of them quoted from its start; they are in F-849's row. One
candidate was disproved before it was numbered: a probe showed the notice over
the page drawn under a floating dock panel on all three engines, but it asked
`elementFromPoint`, which passes over an element with `pointer-events: none`,
and asked again with the notice hit-testable, the notice is on top on all three,
because the workspace isolates its own stacking. The notice's comment says so
now.

### The fifteenth round's dispositions

As before, each test named with the mutation it was proved with: the defect put
back, or the test run against the code before the fix, and seen to fail, then
passing with the code restored. What changed in how that is run, as it is kept
(F-858, F-872, F-889): each Vitest mutation runs the whole test file that holds
its test, and counts as caught only where every test it names is among the
failures; each group of mutations carries one control, a reworded comment in a
file the group mutates, run against every test file any defect of the group
runs against, every one of which must pass; each browser mutation runs the
whole spec file that holds its test, on one project, and a browser control runs
every spec file and project its group's defects run on; the cruiser rules are
proved by running the cruise itself; and every harness hashes the working tree
before its first run and after each, and stops at a difference. No hash
changed. A row with no behaviour to prove says so. In the Proofs below a
quoted string is a test's title; a defect, a sentence or code is in backticks.

| Id | Disposition |

### What the fifteenth round corrects in earlier rows

Thirty-nine corrections, each written where the claim it corrects is:
thirty-six are rows, two are the fourteenth round's preamble and one the
fourteenth round's dispositions. This record is append-only, so a row keeps
what it said and the correction says what is known now. The six paragraphs in
which the fourteenth round wrote past eighty columns are re-flowed, with not a
word changed (F-891). Three more corrections were written into earlier proof
logs, which are not part of this record and are counted in none of these
numbers: two in the thirteenth round's, for the fallback mutation's result and
for a state it said no tree could hold (F-888), and one in the fourteenth
round's, for a comparison it said was made and two mutations run over an
evidence edited after them (F-889). Each is appended, and nothing in either
log was rewritten.

## The sixteenth round, over the fifteenth remediation

`contracts/review-gates.md` step 6 again. The seven lenses ran read-only
against `155382b`, with the packet, the requirements, this record, the evidence
and the resume note, and were asked to verify the fifteenth round's
dispositions, its thirty-nine corrections and its counts against the code, and
to find what the fifteenth remediation had introduced. Numbered from F-894, a
defect found by more than one lens being one finding with the lenses listed
together. Each lens's report and the proof log of this round were kept outside
the tree as they were written, and are the source of every count and proof
below. The Adversarial lens ran twice: its report is the second run's, which
checked each finding of the first against the tree before keeping it and added
four of its own.

Counted from the reports, a finding once for each lens that raised it, at the
grade it was reported at. Sixty-five reported findings — two MEDIUM,
twenty-nine LOW and thirty-four NOTE, none BLOCKER, CRITICAL or HIGH — merge
into forty, F-894 to F-933: two MEDIUM, twenty-one LOW and seventeen NOTE. No
finding was numbered from the round's own work. The merges are these, sixteen
of them, saving twenty-five rows, each with its lenses in the order of the
table above:
